challenges.name: restaurant-page-loader
challenges.title: Remove the restaurant page waterfall
challenges.description: The restaurant page of Rice Rocket's Next.js app awaited five requests one after another (restaurant, menu, cart, reviews, recommendations): about 940 ms before anything could render, and the hero image only started downloading after all of them. The editor holds `app/restaurants/[slug]/load.js` with its blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: every request that needs only the slug starts at once; the recommendations start the moment the menu's category ids are known; the hero image is preloaded the moment the restaurant's data arrives; the reviews start as soon as the restaurant id is known but the loader does not wait for them (it returns them as a promise for a `<Suspense>` boundary); and each endpoint is called once. Run executes the loader against a fake API on a virtual clock and reports when each request started and when the page was ready.
hints: Draw the dependency graph: which requests need nothing but the slug, which need data from another response, and which does the first paint not need at all?

A promise starts its work when you call the function, not when you `await` it. Keep the promises in variables, chain dependent calls with `.then`, and `await Promise.all([...])` only what must be ready.

A product page with a deferred Q&A section looks like: `const productP = api.product(id); const priceP = api.price(id); const similarP = productP.then((p) => api.similar(p.categoryId)); const qaP = productP.then((p) => api.questions(p.sku)); const [product, price, similar] = await Promise.all([productP, priceP, similarP]); return { product, price, similar, questions: qaP };`

tests.name: The page is ready at 330 ms with the restaurant, menu, cart and recommendations
A slow menu delays only the menu and recommendations; reviews still stream at 520 ms
Slow reviews (2 s) never hold back the first paint
